title: A Podcast on What Sincerity Really Means
script: Host: [warmly] Welcome back to the show. Today my guest is Ilham, who wants to talk about sincerity, or ikhlas. Thanks for joining me.
Guest: [pleasantly] Thank you for having me. This topic changed my life a few years ago, so I'm glad to talk about it.
Host: [curious] For listeners who are unfamiliar, how would you explain sincerity in simple words?
Guest: [thoughtful] I would say sincerity means doing something good for Allah's sake alone, not for praise, not for image, not even for a good feeling.
Host: [interested] That sounds difficult to actually live out. Was there a moment that taught you this?
Guest: [reflective] Yes. A few years ago, I used to post about every good deed I did online, without even noticing the habit.
Host: [curious] What made you notice it?
Guest: [honestly] One day, I helped an elderly neighbor carry groceries, and my very first thought was, I should post this.
Host: [surprised] That's a very honest thing to admit.
Guest: [gently] It embarrassed me, actually. I realized the deed had quietly become about me, not about helping her.
Host: [curious] So what did you change after that?
Guest: [warmly] I started doing small good things and deliberately telling no one, not even my closest friends.
Host: [interested] Was that hard at first?
Guest: [honestly] Extremely hard. I kept wanting to mention it, almost out of habit, like an itch I had to scratch.
Host: [curious] Does it feel easier now?
Guest: [reflective] A little. But honestly, I think this is a lifelong practice, not something you finish and master completely.
Host: [thoughtful] What would you tell someone who struggles with wanting recognition for good deeds?
Guest: [encouraging] I would say, notice the urge without judging yourself too harshly, and gently choose quiet instead, again and again.
Host: [smiling] That's a beautiful, honest note to end on, Ilham. Thank you for sharing your story with us today.
Guest: [warmly] Thank you for listening. I hope it helps someone notice their own quiet urge for recognition too.
